title: Exploded View of a Belt-Driven Centrifugal Fan
description: Interactive exploded view of a belt-driven SWSI centrifugal fan, Arrangement 9. Explore mode opens an infobox for each of 14 parts and can assemble and explode the drawing; quiz mode hides the labels and asks 10 identification prompts with two attempts each, then reports the first-attempt score against a mastery level of 9 of 10. The drawing is a simplified schematic modeled on FanPedia page 10, not to scale.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of a belt-driven centrifugal fan (Arrangement 9)
learningObjectives: The learner will identify each of the 14 labeled parts in an exploded view of a belt-driven Arrangement 9 centrifugal fan when given the part's name or function.

accessibility.notes: Every part is a focusable role=button (Tab, then Enter or Space); after an answer focus moves to Next, so Enter goes on. Verdicts, prompts and the summary are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an "Answer" badge pair with colour. During the quiz part names are hidden from screen readers too ("Part k") until revealed. SVG label text scales with the drawing and is about 13 px at an 800 px wide frame.

rules: Explore mode: selecting any part opens its infobox; one infobox is open at a time; opened parts are marked visited.
Quiz mode: 10 prompts in a fixed order, one selection per prompt per attempt, two attempts each; a prompt is correct only when the exact part in the spec's Correct part column is selected.
A second miss highlights the correct part and the prompt counts as missed.
Score: correct on first attempt, n of 10; mastery is 9 of 10.
assumptions: The flanged inlet is drawn in a separate Inlet option box because a fan ships with either an inlet collar or a flanged inlet, not both.
limitations: Simplified oblique schematic drawn in code; not to scale and not a specific Twin City Fan model.

sources: FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, page 10 (exploded view, belt-driven centrifugal fans, Arrangement 9)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled-diagram exploration followed by retrieval practice (identify the part from a name or function)
keyQuestions: Which part adds energy to the air?
Which inlet part shapes the air, and which ones only connect the duct?
Which parts of an Arrangement 9 fan sit outside the airstream?
Which part would you change to change fan speed?
commonMisconceptions: The inlet funnel and inlet collar are the same part (the funnel shapes the air into the impeller; the collar is a duct connection).
The pedestal is part of the housing (it is a separate support for the bearings and shaft).
The sheave on the fan shaft is the same size as the motor sheave (their ratio sets fan speed).
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'Correct on first attempt: n of 10'; mastery is 9 of 10 on the first attempt.
Summary list of missed prompts and prompts correct on the second attempt, each with the reason for the correct answer.
